questions.question: What does demand describe?
choices: Only the amount consumers wish existed
Quantities sellers can produce without buyers
Quantities buyers are willing and able to buy at different prices
Only a product's production expenses

questions.question: What does supply describe?
choices: Quantities sellers are willing and able to offer at different prices
Only the goods already purchased by consumers
The income of households after taxes
The amount government must buy by law

questions.question: What does the law of demand generally predict, other things equal?
choices: A higher price always increases quantity demanded
A higher price leads to a lower quantity demanded
A price change leaves quantity demanded unchanged
A lower price always reduces quantity demanded

questions.question: What does the law of supply generally predict, other things equal?
choices: A higher price always reduces quantity supplied
A price change automatically shifts the entire supply curve
A lower price always increases quantity supplied
A higher price leads to a higher quantity supplied

questions.question: What is equilibrium in a market?
choices: A price where quantity supplied equals quantity demanded
A price where no trade occurs
A price chosen only by the largest buyer
A price where demand is always zero

questions.question: What is a shortage at a given price?
choices: Quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded
Every buyer has purchased the desired quantity
Quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied
Supply and demand curves are identical

questions.question: What is a surplus at a given price?
choices: Quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied
Quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded
The market has no sellers
The market has no available goods

questions.question: What causes movement along a demand curve?
choices: A change in buyers' tastes
A change in buyers' income
A change in the number of buyers
A change in the good's own price

questions.question: How does an increase in production costs usually affect supply?
choices: It decreases supply at a given price
It increases supply at every price
It increases demand directly
It leaves supply unchanged by definition

questions.question: For a normal good, how does a rise in consumer income usually affect demand?
choices: Demand decreases
Supply increases directly
Demand increases
Quantity supplied becomes zero

questions.question: If the price of a substitute rises, what generally happens to demand for the original good?
choices: Demand decreases
Demand increases
The original good's supply curve must shift left
The original good becomes a public good

questions.question: If a complement becomes more expensive, what generally happens to demand for the original good?
choices: Demand increases
Supply always doubles
The market's production costs disappear
Demand decreases

questions.question: What does a technological improvement usually do to supply?
choices: It increases supply if production becomes less costly
It decreases demand by definition
It fixes prices permanently
It removes all production constraints

questions.question: What tends to happen to price when a shortage persists in an otherwise competitive market without price controls?
choices: Downward pressure develops
Price must remain unchanged by definition
Upward pressure develops
The demand curve must become horizontal

questions.question: Why must other factors be held constant when applying the law of demand?
choices: Consumers never change their tastes
Other changes can also affect purchases
All products have identical demand
Only government purchases matter

questions.question: Demand increases while supply stays unchanged. What is the usual equilibrium effect?
choices: Lower price and lower quantity
Higher price and lower quantity
Lower price and higher quantity
Higher price and higher quantity

questions.question: Supply increases while demand stays unchanged. What is the usual equilibrium effect?
choices: Lower price and higher quantity
Higher price and higher quantity
Lower price and lower quantity
Higher price and lower quantity

questions.question: A drought reduces the apple harvest. Which change best represents this?
choices: A rightward shift of apple demand caused directly by drought
Movement along unchanged supply caused only by a lower price
A leftward shift of apple supply
An increase in the number of apple sellers

questions.question: A product's price falls and buyers purchase more, with other factors unchanged. What occurred?
choices: An increase in demand shifting the curve
An increase in quantity demanded along the curve
A decrease in supply shifting the curve
A decrease in quantity demanded along the curve

questions.question: Both demand and supply increase. What can be concluded without knowing their relative sizes?
choices: Equilibrium price necessarily rises
Equilibrium quantity necessarily falls
Equilibrium price necessarily falls
Equilibrium quantity rises, but the price change is uncertain
